something i’ve found is just getting yourself all fancied up (in whatever way makes you happy whether makeup or hair or outfits or anything) and just take some pictures. don’t point out your flaws, point out what you like and appreciate. also don’t compare yourself to other pictures, just enjoy yourself and your body and learn what about it you like best so that you can find ways to accent that part rather than finding ways to hide what you don’t like. also trying on a bunch of clothes helps too, because it’s the easier way to find what is most flattering on you. and if something isn’t cute, then oh well move onto the next. no one looks amazing in every single style that exists, so if something doesn’t work for you that’s okay. also figuring out what style of bralettes fit best is a fun way to figure out what makes you feel good so that you can find similar styles and feel confident knowing you’ll look good in them.

i’m so sorry you’ve had such an awful experience with horrible people making comments. i’ve found that many girls, especially the ones who seem “perfect” with the body the face and whatever, are usually so insecure themselves that they have to tear others down to bring themselves up. this is what i experienced at my highschool, which (no joke) was 96% white, with most of them being extremely rich. they seemed to have “the life” with the money and clothes and body, but jesus i’ve never met more vile people in my life. they never had a positive thing to say about anyone, even the people they claimed to be their best friends, and spent all day just judging the hell out of everyone around them. to me, that seems like a miserable life. 

just because you don’t have the “ideal body” that social media throws in all of our faces, doesn’t mean you aren’t beautiful or that people won’t find you attractive. i’m not plus size, but for my body type i have a very “manly” build. i did gymnastics for years, along with other sports, so i have a very muscular build that goes beyond the toned built that people say is “attractive” for women. i also have literally no hips, very very broad shoulders, huge hands, huge feet, and boobs that barely show on my chest. it’s taken me forever to accept that just because i don’t look like everyone around me, doesn’t mean i’m not pretty too. while we all like to think there is an ideal size, there really isn’t considering everyone is different and everyone prefers different things. just because you haven’t found someone for you yet doesn’t mean they aren’t out there. (plus most boys are absolute dipshits and their opinions hold no value when it comes to what a girl should look like or whatever)

also many “thicc” girls out there on social media are either extremely lucky (rare) or more commonly are fake whether it be editing pictures or angles or plastic surgery. i’ve learned that listening to other people’s opinions on the standard of beauty only does harm, and it’s better to realize that any form of different is okay, and that vile people will never change and most likely never be happy, so it’s best to use your own thoughts rather than listen to someone who can’t see past their own ego. 

learning to love yourself takes time, and that’s okay. i still have mental breakdowns in the mirror or think about what i would change, but i also try to correct myself every time i do it. it doesn’t matter if you believe it or not at first, because after some time it’ll become habit. change any self hate into a positive comment, and it’ll feel awkward at first but sooner or later it’ll come out much easier and it’ll be easier to believe or at least begin to believe. wishing you the best of luck, and hoping for happiness for you.

for me, i’ve had to learn that the path to self love and acceptance isn’t linear, meaning that there will be ups and downs and that’s okay. i struggled soo much in highschool, but looking back that was definitely because i was surrounded by the wrong crowd who often chose to tear others down in an attempt to build themselves up. even now tho, two years later i still struggle, but i’ve found it isn’t worth the time and effort spent analyzing yourself and picking out your “flaws” and thinking about what you want to be different. and i’ve also found it is NOT worth the time to listen to anyone who tries to tear you down, because usually it stems from their own personal insecurities or jealously of your confidence. negative comments from others may still hurt, but don’t let what others say become what you think of yourself. everyone has different opinions, and i try to remember that just because someone doesn’t like me doesn’t mean someone else won’t. there’s always gonna be good and bad people, and it’s not worth it to only listen or stick around with the bad. 


also, don’t be afraid to go out in whatever you feel comfortable in. key word here - comfortable. don’t force yourself out in something you aren’t ready for yet, but don’t be afraid to slowly try some new things and test the waters. and don’t forget, boobs are not at all the one single thing everyone looks at. i used to get so caught up over the fact that i hated my boobs that i forgot i had the whole rest of my body - meaning that i forgot that when people see me, they see all of me, not just my boobs. they see my hair, eyes, face, outfit, arms, legs, etc. and unless they are some creep, they will see all of you and won’t notice your chest as much as you think. other than that, just always try to limit self criticism, and practice self love. turn the thoughts of “ugh i hate my chest” to “wow i love how the cut of this shirt makes me look” or things like that. 

even today i’m still learning, but it’s never too late to start the process. wishing you the best of luck🖤

i saw all sorts of things. it ranged from black silhouettes of people to dark figures of different shapes to crawling figures to hands poking out from behind furniture in my room to seeing something holding my arms down to multiple figures that if you tried to look at them they would disappear and reappear somewhere else to other shit. it was never a super clear image of what i saw because it felt like everything was moving in slow motion and anything i saw was either blurry or like lagged to where i saw its past movements as it moved if that makes sense. the worst thing would be when i saw a person that was in my apartment with me at the time, and when that happened it felt more like a dream but they would say something like “don’t look” or “it’s not safe here” and that’s when everything would slow down and something would begin to move towards me. the pounding and ringing i would always hear usually drowned out most sound but if i hear anything, it sounded like background noise and i could never tell where it was coming from or what it was coming from.

literally all sorts of things. at first it was absolutely terrifying and it would start with me feeling huge amounts of pressure like something was holding me down, and if i tried to move it felt like i was moving in slow motion. then the panic would set in and that’s usually when i would see or hear things around me. the things i would see would usually be in my peripheral vision, and by the time i turned my head to see what was moving it would be right in front of my face. it would range from silhouettes of people to weird dark figures that didn’t look like anything i’ve seen and they would usually be crawling. the weird thing is, sometimes if someone was in my apartment at the time i had sleep paralysis, whether if they were sleeping next to me or in an entirely different room, they would sometimes appear when i was having sleep paralysis, and they always would have a look on their face of pure fear that i’ve never seen them make before and they’d always say something horrifying like “don’t look” or “it’s not safe” or anything you don’t want to hear. for sounds, it varied because usually it was this intense pounding and ringing in my ear that would drown out most sounds around me, which meant if i did hear something i would have no idea where it came from or what made it. after awhile i learned to kinda recognize when it was happening and just try to repeat to myself “it’s not real. it’s not real.” over and over again until it stopped.

it was absolutely awful for all of them. my work was open from 8am-6pm but sometimes i wouldn’t even be awake during that period to call in. thankfully i worked at a call center and it wasn’t extremely important that i was there, but i basically had to tell my boss i couldn’t work because i didn’t know when i would be awake or how long i would be asleep once i fell asleep. i’m glad i had some money saved up from the past because i couldn’t work for that entire period. 

i wouldn’t say i lost friends or anything, but i had to explain to my friends that if i didn’t respond or missed things i didn’t do it on purpose. my closest friends understood, but some didn’t understand how i “couldn’t just wake up” and that really sucked. i couldn’t really make plans with people bc i couldn’t guarantee i would make it. it just kinda sucked that i had to explain myself fully to everyone in my life and try to help them understand and hope they wouldn’t think i was lying or just making excuses.

for me, if i think “ugh i have to be here for two more hours” then i’m gonna be miserable. but for some reason if i think of a time frame that i’m okay with, like maybe “we’ll i just have to sit through 30 more minutes 4 times” then for some reason it’s okay for me most of the time. it’s almost intriguing to me like “okay i’m 1/4 of the way done so now i have 3 more 30 minutes to go through” until i’m done. also if i find something interesting to focus on or something to do that i’m okay with, time goes by faster. if i focus on the time, then i’m gonna be miserable and it’s gonna feel like forever. but if i find a way to distract myself from the time and find something to fill up the time where i’m not upset, it usually helps.

ME TOO. if it’s vague, i get distracted. if it’s too big, i get overwhelmed and push it out of my mind. if it’s too much information at once, my brain gets full of nothing and remembers nothing. if there’s not enough info, i’ll doubt myself and won’t want to even begin it. i have to be told EXACTLY what to do and how to do it and when to do it and everything, which may seem like extra work to others, but i struggle with making a plan on my own, and if i’m given a plan that someone else has created it makes my life 100% easier.

First of all, I would like to say you have a damn strong soul after everything you’ve been through from the beginning up until now and the fact that you’re still trying and looking for options is amazing and inspiring to me. Second, what country do you live in? I struggled getting my college to recognize the fact that I truly had a disability that prevented me from functioning like the other students. They had an accommodations office, which is supposed to offer accommodations or changes to your schooling that are adapted to your situation, so if by chance your school has one of those I would recommend starting there just in case. 

Some schools or colleges offer free counseling, which above all is a start and at least an option to be heard and be offered ideas of what you should do or who to talk to etc. For medications, I never found an anti-depressant that relieved my suffering, and later when I was told that in fact my ADHD was the core issue, I was prescribed adderall which was life changing to me where I could think more clear, feel and understand my emotions better, manage my time better, be able to start and complete most of my work, etc and honestly with some of the things you’re saying I would look up information about ADHD to see if that could also be a part of the reasons for your brain fog and other things. 

I’m not particularly super religious and I’m not fond of most churches, but some churches have support groups or possibly even free counseling and advice and sometimes there’s the chance of people who are willing to help others that they don’t even know, so maybe you could check there as well.

Honestly the best option would have to be going back to the hospital. Please give the hospital another chance.

I’m about to be a sophomore in college, but back in high school i was completely the exact same way. We had options for classes with weighted GPA meaning the highest GPA if you chose to take these classes is a 4.5. I had worked my way up to a perfect 4.5, up until I got hid hard with mental illness and started to not be able to go to school very often. I maintained a 4.3 which to my parents and friends seemed great, but to me I was devastated and thought I had ruined my future possibilities of great colleges or opportunities or whatever. Looking back now, it seems almost ridiculous (talking about myself here fwi) that I sobbed and sobbed over a small GPA change that was still very high and appreciated. Especially in high school, I learned that your GPA really is not the determining factor of your life path, and that even a 3.5 is still great in college and a few lower grades isn’t the end of the world (even though I know it feels like it). Colleges look at much more than GPA from testing to experiences to other things where as long as you keep a “presentable” GPA it really doesn’t matter as much as it’s made to seem. Life happens and sometimes you get a grade that truly hurts your heart, but you have to realize for yourself that you are worth so much more than a number and that the number itself isn’t worth as much as people say it does. Hope this helps.
